what_it_does: Safety-critical chips — think automotive or industrial controllers — often use a technique called lockstep, where two copies of the same processor run the same instructions simultaneously so any discrepancy reveals a hardware error. The problem is that lockstep is all-or-nothing: you dedicate a whole extra core to error-checking even when a task does not need that level of protection, wasting compute in systems where some tasks need high reliability and others do not. FlexStep proposes hardware that lets cores be dynamically paired or un-paired as checkers on demand, depending on which task is currently running and how critical it is. The operating system (the software that manages tasks) orchestrates these reconfigurations, enabling a mixed fleet of tasks with different reliability needs to share the same cores efficiently. The abstract indicates this reduces over-provisioning without sacrificing safety where it matters.
